Virtual Resection is a technique for selectively suppressing portions of a volume dataset to resolve occlusion problems, particularly in medical imaging where internal structures (e.g., pulmonary nodules) are hidden by surrounding tissue (e.g., lung parenchyma) [S2].

The claim states that Virtual Resection is a technique for selectively suppressing portions of a volume dataset to resolve occlusion problems, particularly in medical imaging where internal structures (e.g., pulmonary nodules) are hidden by surrounding tissue (e.g., lung parenchyma). Source [S2] explicitly describes a computational framework using 'selective volume clipping' (a form of virtual resection) to solve the 'occlusion problem between lungs and pulmonary nodules in chest CT images.' It details how lung tissue is cut around nodules to allow visualization of the nodules while preserving the texture of the lung surface, which aligns perfectly with the claim's description of resolving occlusion where internal structures are hidden by surrounding tissue.
